name: default-image-mutability-policy
description: Mutability classification and prioritisation policy for container image references. Scanners are policy-agnostic; everything opinionated lives here.
_acceptable_note: The boundary drawn by the source playbook: codename and version tags are acceptable, anything with no version component is not. Every report states this so reviewers argue with the policy, not the data.
_codename_note: A codename names a fixed OS release: patch-mutable, but not a moving track like :latest. Separated from versionless variants (:alpine, :slim), which pin nothing.
_abandoned_note: Flagged regardless of tag class. A digest-pinned image from an unmaintained namespace is still a supply-chain risk; pinning does not address abandonment.
_finding_flags_note: Which ownership flags are findings in their own right. abandoned_namespace is: the namespace is known-dead. unverified_namespace is NOT: it describes most of Docker Hub, and promoting every such image to a finding would bury the unpinned ones. It goes to a watch list and annotates findings it touches.
_self_exclude_note: A scanner's own fixtures, policy and docs legitimately contain every pattern it hunts for, so scanning them reports the tool to itself. supply-chain-ioc-scan learned this first ('exclude your own tooling and transcripts'). Exclusions are COUNTED and listed in the report - a silent exclusion is how a real finding disappears.
_org_owned_note: Images in registries the org controls may be excluded from remediation - but org images on public Docker Hub are only as safe as that account's credentials, which is exactly what these worms steal. Empty by default: opting out is a deliberate act.

priority_rules.why: composite action, runs in CI with credentials
developer machines - the actual blast radius of token-stealing worms

_priority_note: Ordered; first match wins. Repo-level overrides (archived repos to P2) are applied before these by the scanner, since they are a property of the repository rather than the path.
_infra_template_note: Applied when the FILE CONTENT sniffs as CloudFormation (AWSTemplateFormatVersion, or a resource's Type: AWS::...), independent of every path_glob rule above and independent of directory naming convention. A real org run found a docker reference inside a CFN template that fell through to the P1 default because no glob named the directory it happened to live in - the same class of gap *.tf closes for Terraform, generalised by content instead of extension.
_archived_note: The correct fix for an archived repo is usually archiving harder - deleting it - not editing it.

known_benign_collisions._key_names_note: A generic `reference:` key collided with 800+ dbt column definitions in the original run. Excluded structurally: only keys whose name contains 'image' are treated as image keys.
known_benign_collisions._value_note: Ansible AMI ids, asset paths, URLs and template expressions are not image references. A template expression is recorded as a residual blind spot rather than a finding: the real value is composed elsewhere.

_template_note: A reference containing one of these is composed at deploy time. It is reported as UNRESOLVED, never as clean: a scanner that cannot see the value must not imply it checked it.
